definition: Relationship conflict is trouble or disagreement within a close relationship. In the mental health context, it can act as a source of stress and may make symptoms worse at times.

reasons: The packet only uses “family or relationship conflict” as an example of a stressful situation; it does not define relationship conflict as “trouble or disagreement within a close relationship.”
The statement that relationship conflict “can act as a source of stress” is supported only as a contextual example in the GAD publication, not as a general definition of the term.

The wording adds “may make symptoms worse at times” as a general meaning, but the packet supports this only for GAD symptoms during times of stress, not as a standalone definition of relationship conflict.
The packet does not define “relationship conflict” as “trouble or disagreement within a close relationship.” It only refers to “a family or relationship conflict” as an example of a stressful time.

While the packet supports that symptoms may be worse “during times of stress—for example…a family or relationship conflict” (i.e., making symptoms worse at times in the context of GAD), the first sentence and the broader claim that relationship conflict can generally act as a source of stress in mental health are not directly established by the provided text.
